en.question: Which flights are covered by EU 261?
en.answer: The rules cover every flight departing from an airport in the EU, whatever the airline. They also cover flights from outside the EU to an EU airport when the airline is licensed in the EU.
en.how: Iceland, Norway and Switzerland apply the same rules. A flight from New York to Stockholm on a US airline is not covered, while the same route on an EU airline is.

en.answer: Compensation is 250 euro for flights up to 1,500 km, 400 euro for flights within the EU over 1,500 km and other flights of 1,500 to 3,500 km, and 600 euro for all other flights. The amount is per passenger and does not depend on the ticket price.
en.how: The amount may be cut by half if the airline offers another flight that arrives no more than two, three or four hours late, depending on distance. Distance is measured as the great circle distance to the final destination.

en.answer: A flight counts as arrived when at least one aircraft door opens and passengers may leave. Touchdown on the runway is not the arrival time.

en.question: Do I get compensation if the airline cancels two weeks before?
en.answer: No. If you are told at least 14 days before departure, there is no compensation, though you keep the right to a refund or another flight. Notice between 7 and 14 days, or under 7 days, only removes compensation if the new flight is close to the original times.
en.how: With 7 to 14 days notice the new flight may leave at most two hours earlier and arrive at most four hours later. With under 7 days notice the limits are one hour earlier and two hours later.

en.answer: As a rule, no. Technical problems that come from the normal operation of the aircraft are the airline's risk, so compensation is still owed.
